vignette: Lata, a 67-year-old South Asian woman and non-profit worker, has been struggling with the aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred several months ago. Married for over four decades, Lata’s life was thrown into turmoil following the traumatic event. The attack happened one evening as she walked home from her office in downtown Chicago. She had just finished an exhausting day at work and was looking forward to spending some quality time with her husband. However, her peace was shattered when a stranger attacked her on an isolated street. Since that night, Lata has been haunted by the memory of the assault. The trauma has left her feeling vulnerable and unsafe in public spaces, particularly streets she once walked freely without fear. She now avoids walking alone at night and often takes extra precautions like carrying pepper spray or sticking to well-lit areas. Her daily routine has become significantly impacted as she refrains from going out unless absolutely necessary. Her husband has noticed the change in Lata's behavior and is concerned about her constant state of anxiety. He supports her but feels helpless when she becomes distressed at unexpected moments, often triggered by sounds or situations that remind her of the assault. For instance, the sight of an alleyway similar to where the attack occurred can send her into a panic. Lata’s work as a non-profit worker has also been affected. She used to be very active in organizing community events and attending meetings after hours. Now, she avoids these activities because they often involve being out late or traveling alone, which triggers flashbacks of the assault. Her colleagues have noticed her withdrawal but do not know the underlying reason. Despite her efforts to avoid reminders of the trauma, Lata finds herself constantly monitoring her surroundings for potential threats. She is hyper-aware of every shadow and sound in public spaces, making it difficult for her to relax or enjoy simple activities like going to a park or attending social gatherings with friends from work. This heightened state of vigilance has taken a toll on her mental health, leading to frequent insomnia and persistent feelings of fear. What frightens Lata most is the prospect that she might never feel safe again. She fears that she will continue to be haunted by memories of the assault and that her life will be defined by the trauma. Her husband has been encouraging her to seek help, but until recently, she had hesitated out of a sense of shame and fear that speaking about it would only make things worse. Lata finally decided to seek professional help after an incident at work where she experienced a severe panic attack during a routine meeting. She realized then that the trauma was not something she could manage on her own anymore. Her primary hope is to regain a sense of normalcy and safety, to be able to go out without fear and live her life without being constantly reminded of the assault. Her journey into therapy marks a critical step towards reclaiming her peace and regaining control over her daily life. Lata's determination and support from her husband make it clear that she is committed to finding the tools to heal and move forward.
